[LLEX.8.1.1] Multi-character operator tokens follow the longest-match rule:
the lexer emits the longest operator string starting at the
current position.

| Precedes | Longer form (emitted if next char matches) |
|---|---|
| `-` | `->` |
| `*` | `**` |
| `/` | `//` |
| `<` | `<=`, `<<` |
| `>` | `>=`, `>>` |
| `=` | `==` |
| `!` | `!=`, `!~` (lone `!` is a lexer error) |
| `:` | `::` |
| `?` | `??` |
| `.` | `..` |
| `"` | `"""` (if followed by two more `"`; else single `"` opens a `SINGLE_STR`) |
